clue.text: Important to subscribe if I'm not able to

parts.note: to subscribe is to sign your name
taken as written
I'm not able to is I can't, written without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone protests that a signature matters even when they cannot give it.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one sentence about signing; 'I'm not able to' is the contraction I can't, apostrophe dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: Something significant carries weight or meaning, a close synonym of important.

clue.text: Safe to go round in Europe with cushy job?

indicators.note: to go round says the safe word is wrapped around the other pieces

parts.note: sure means safe, as in a sure bet
taken as written
EC, the European Community, stands for Europe

explanation.surface: Someone seeks a secure, easy job somewhere in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go round' wraps the safe word around the other two pieces. EC, the European Community, is a standard crossword abbreviation for Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: A sinecure is a post paying a salary while asking little or no work, an easy position.

clue.text: Pleasure-seeking but well-behaved age

parts.note: good means well-behaved
an age is an era or time

explanation.surface: Someone is both a hedonist and well-behaved in old age.
explanation.definitionFit: Good-time describes a person devoted to fun and enjoyment.

clue.text: Best one has wood underneath

indicators.note: underneath says the wood goes below the one in this down answer

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
deal is pine or fir timber

explanation.surface: The finest item has a wooden base.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'has wood underneath' puts DEAL below I.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideal means perfect, the best possible.

clue.text: Bowling technique all the rage with southern side

parts.note: fashionable is in
a wing is a side, of a building or a team

explanation.surface: A cricket technique that is fashionable for a team from the south.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the inswing is a delivery that curves in towards the batsman in the air.
explanation.definitionFit: Inswing is a bowler's method of making the ball curve into the batsman, a cricket skill.

clue.text: Is able in the morning with the French to go over calendar

indicators.note: to go over means to turn over, so the whole string of pieces is read backwards

parts.note: is able means can
AM, ante meridiem, means in the morning
la is a French word for the

explanation.surface: Someone capable in the morning goes through a calendar in French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go over' turns the whole run CAN + AM + LA backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An almanac is a yearly publication with a calendar of dates and events.

clue.text: Permissible variation possibly not clear to English

indicators.note: possibly says the letters of the next two words might be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: An engineer warns that the allowed margin may not be clear to the English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges the two words 'not clear', and the abbreviation for English then follows.
explanation.definitionFit: In engineering a tolerance is the allowed range of deviation in a measurement.

clue.text: Starts to regret ignoring broken bone

indicators.note: starts to tells us to take the opening letter of each of the next three words

explanation.surface: Someone tries not to regret a fractured bone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starts to' picks the first letters of regret, ignoring and broken.
explanation.definitionFit: A rib is one of the curved bones of the chest, so it is an example of a bone.

clue.text: For sale note on rear section

indicators.note: on says the note sits on top of the rear section in this down answer

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
a tail is a rear part

explanation.surface: A notice on the back of something says it is for sale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'note' looks like a written message; in crosswords it is a sol-fa note, here RE.
explanation.definitionFit: Retail is selling goods directly to the public, so up for sale in a shop.

clue.text: Boycott gets his off drive away

parts.note: to boycott is to ban

indicators.note: off means wrong or out of order, so the letters of his are jumbled

explanation.surface: Geoffrey Boycott, the Yorkshire batsman, plays his off drive.
explanation.walkthrough: Boycott is a famous English cricketer and an off drive a cricket shot, which hides the verb 'boycott' and the anagram signal 'off'.
explanation.definitionFit: To banish is to send away or expel.

clue.text: A quarter after twelve and not a single person

indicators.note: after says the quarter is written following the twelve

parts.note: twelve o'clock midday is noon
a quarter is one of the four compass points; here east, E

explanation.surface: At a quarter past twelve the place is empty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A quarter' looks like fifteen minutes on the clock, but crosswords use it for a compass point: here E for east.
explanation.definitionFit: Nobody at all: no one means not a single individual.

clue.text: Easy time playing the fool

parts.note: easy means simple
an actor who is playing is on, on stage

explanation.surface: An actor has a simple job when cast as the fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playing the fool' reads as one idea, but 'playing' gives ON and 'the fool' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A simpleton is a foolish, gullible person, so a synonym of a fool.

clue.text: In bed poorly — no one to go over old French dance

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
poorly means ill

indicators.note: to go over means to turn over, so the words no and one are read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: Someone ill in bed with nobody to rehearse an old French dance with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go over' turns NO + I round to give ION.
explanation.definitionFit: The cotillion was an eighteenth-century French social dance for couples in a square, a forerunner of the quadrille.

clue.text: Small birds make tracks

explanation.surface: Little birds leave footprints behind them.
explanation.definitionFit: Rails are small marsh birds such as the water rail; rails are also the metal bars of a railway track.

clue.text: Possible source of mutton served on fine china with stuffing

indicators.note: served on says the meat sits on top of the china, first in this down-reading order

parts.note: mutton is sheep meat and a ram is a male sheep, hence only a possible source
Ming porcelain, from the Chinese Ming dynasty, is the classic fine china

explanation.surface: A menu offers mutton on Ming porcelain, with a stuffing.
explanation.walkthrough: The menu picture makes 'stuffing' look like a side dish; it is the definition, and 'served on' places the meat first in this down-reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramming something into a space means cramming it in, so stuffing.

clue.text: Bring in a French hound

parts.note: to import is to bring in goods
une is the French feminine for a

explanation.surface: Someone brings a French hunting dog into the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hound' looks like a dog; it is the verb meaning to pester.
explanation.definitionFit: To importune is to harass with persistent requests, to badger.

clue.text: Variety of sugar beet, so to speak

explanation.surface: A lesson in sugar types: is beet just another kind?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Variety of sugar beet' reads as one plant; split it after 'sugar'. 'So to speak' says beet is heard as beat, and to beat a child once meant to give them the cane.
explanation.definitionFit: Sugar cane is a kind of sugar crop; to cane someone is to beat them with a stick.

clue.text: Bitter drunk: look round for words set to music

indicators.note: round says the look word goes around the jumbled bitter

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters of bitter staggering into a new order

explanation.surface: After drinking bitter beer, someone looks around for song lyrics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' scrambles the beer word, and 'round' wraps the old word for look around that scramble.
explanation.definitionFit: A libretto is the text of an opera or musical.

clue.text: Sea egret wanders into shipboard accommodation

indicators.note: wanders suggests the letters of sea egret roaming into a new order

explanation.surface: A sea bird strays into the cheap quarters of a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanders' rearranges SEA EGRET.
explanation.definitionFit: Steerage was the cheapest passenger section on a ship.

clue.text: Strip of sand? You could put odds on it

definitions.text: You could put odds on it

explanation.surface: A gambler eyes a sandbank and talks about betting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put odds on' suggests betting; read it as putting odds and ends of meat on a skewer for roasting.
explanation.definitionFit: A spit is a narrow point of land running into the sea; a spit is also the rod on which meat is roasted.

clue.text: Going off the bend

explanation.surface: Someone is going round the bend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going off the bend' reads as going mad; split it into two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Milk turning is going sour, going off; a turning is also a bend or side road.

clue.text: He dispenses with science, missing the line at the end

indicators.note: missing, with 'at the end', says the line's letters are dropped from the tail of the science

parts.note: chemistry is one of the sciences
RY, for railway, is the crossword abbreviation for a line

explanation.surface: A man gets by without science, giving up the last line of his work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He dispenses with science' reads as rejecting science, but 'He dispenses' alone is the definition. 'missing ... at the end' drops RY from the end of CHEMISTRY.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a chemist is a pharmacist, the person who makes up and hands out prescriptions.

clue.text: Church start to inveigh against drink

indicators.note: start to says take just the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: anti means against

explanation.surface: A church begins to preach against drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Chianti is a red wine from Tuscany.

clue.text: Smart salesman has to tramp all over

indicators.note: all over says both pieces together are turned around

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative
to pad is to walk heavily, to tramp

explanation.surface: A smartly dressed salesman has to walk everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all over' turns REP + PAD backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Dapper means neat and stylish in dress.

clue.text: Over the sea or a navigable lake

parts.note: a broad is one of the Norfolk Broads, lakes in eastern England used for boating

explanation.surface: A traveller crosses either the sea or a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: The Norfolk Broads are a network of navigable lakes and rivers in eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Abroad means in a foreign country, often overseas.

clue.text: Curve in road: head off with warning light

indicators.note: head off tells us to remove the first letter of the word for the road curve

parts.note: camber is the slight arched curve across a road's surface

explanation.surface: A driver warns of a bend ahead, with a light flashing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head off' removes the C from CAMBER. A camber is the crosswise curve, not a bend, which is the false path.
explanation.definitionFit: Amber is the traffic signal between green and red that warns drivers to prepare to stop.

clue.text: Check strength and provide supplementary resources

parts.note: to rein in is to check or restrain
force means strength

explanation.surface: A commander reviews his strength and sends back-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Check strength' reads as a commander inspecting troops, but each word is a separate synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: To reinforce an army is to send it extra troops and supplies, so to add more resources.

clue.text: Even with plenty of money there's only one suit in it

definitions.text: there's only one suit in it

explanation.surface: A rich card player holds one suit only.
explanation.definitionFit: Flush means level; also well supplied with cash; and in poker a hand of cards all of the same suit.

clue.text: In favour of joining together to make a plentiful supply

parts.note: pro means in favour of
fusion is the joining together of things

explanation.surface: A supporter of mergers hopes they will produce abundance.
explanation.definitionFit: A profusion is an abundance, a great quantity of something.

clue.text: Revolutionary feature of powerful transformer

indicators.note: feature of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A rebel is a key part of a mighty electrical transformer.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters are hidden across powerfUL TRAnsformer.
explanation.definitionFit: An ultra is an extremist, someone holding radical or revolutionary views.

clue.text: Street without a bar

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the letter a is taken out of the street word

parts.note: a road is a street

explanation.surface: A street that has no pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without a bar' reads as a street lacking a pub, but 'without' removes A from ROAD and 'bar' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A rod is a long thin bar of metal or wood.

clue.text: Language increased by description of typical national beauty

parts.note: English is a language
rose means went up or increased

explanation.surface: A language gains a phrase for the typical national beauty.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a fair-complexioned, conventionally attractive woman thought typical of England.
